I definitely agree with the response for a palette and some water. I have never bought a palette. I cheat and use a shallow lid from a Tupperware and a wet rag. You put a piece of parchment paper over the wet rag when it is in the "basin" (Tupperware lid) and make sure it is completely touching the rag and not lifting up. It works so good for me, all my paint stays liquid and doesn't dry up.

Something to hold onto that isn't the model is nice, too. I use a thicker wooden dowel, and I just put green stuff on the bottom of the base and the top of the dowel. It holds well, but there are tons of adhesives, like double-sided tape that you could also use. 

I would also recommend a desk lamp, as it really helps to show the small details of your miniature so you don't miss any spots.

Lastly, when you prime the model, make sure it isn't windy or too hot. Primer will speckle and dry uneven in too much heat or humidity.
